findings.title: Bound overrun does not stop further root reservations
findings.description: Reliable actual usage above this reservation's enforced bound is recorded, but settle_budget persists no indication that the bound was violated and reserve_budget checks only aggregate root exhaustion (lines 115-118). A root with limits calls=3/tokens=1000, outstanding calls=1/tokens=100 and settled zero can settle actual calls=1/tokens=101, then successfully reserve another calls=1/tokens=100. The service owner uses these exact functions, so the same sequence succeeds on S27. This violates the packet residual boundary requiring observed actual above bounds to remain recorded and fail closed for further reservation. Current unit and DC overrun tests use actual totals above the root limit; they cannot distinguish bound overrun from ordinary root exhaustion.
findings.requested_change: Persist a task-scoped, fail-closed accounting basis for observed bound overruns atomically with exact S27/S31/S32 and receipt/event/outbox settlement, and deny subsequent reservations even when aggregate root limits still have capacity. Preserve the verified actual, outstanding other reservations, all unrelated planning fields and late-settlement authority restrictions; do not clamp actuals, discard evidence or reopen/terminate intent through settlement.
findings.required_validation: Add deterministic PU and migrated PostgreSQL service/DC cases with actual exceeding one configured reservation bound while the aggregate root remains below every limit. Assert subsequent reservation denial and no bookkeeping/accounting mutation. Cover join/revision/takeover preservation, equality at the bound remaining allowed, repeated settlement, and rollback of the overrun basis with the atomic settlement writes. Retest all sixteen exact checks on a new tested SHA and obtain fresh reviews.

findings.title: Cross-reservation receipt/request uniqueness has no PostgreSQL proof
findings.description: The new natural receipt/request lookup at transactions.py:3982-3994 prevents one verified provider receipt or request identity from settling two different reservations. Existing duplicate/conflicting cases resubmit the same reservation after it is already SETTLED with expected_revision=2. They are rejected at prepare_ledger_change's revision/state checks before the natural identity lookup runs; the same-key cases replay historical S02. No committed test settles a distinct outstanding reservation with a reused receipt_id or provider_request_id, and no cross-row competing settlement exercises S01 serialization of that new lookup. Thus the claimed reliable natural uniqueness is not demonstrated by the selected DC PASS log.
findings.requested_change: Add real migrated PostgreSQL owner-level tests using two distinct permitted outstanding reservations of the same subject/provider. Reuse receipt identity with a different request identity, and request identity with a different receipt identity, independently. Include competing settlements with bounded barriers and observed PostgreSQL blocking so the second contender rechecks the first committed natural identity.
findings.required_validation: For each conflict, assert only one reservation settles, the other retains its entire occupied bound, and S27 counters, exact S31/S32 transition/payload and S02/S03/S04 counts commit once without a second refund. Same-key ACK-loss retry must return the original outcome without mutation; changed actual/accounting evidence must conflict. Run the named complete DC file and all sixteen exact checks on the repaired tested SHA; rereview the new committed implementation/result.
